abstract: Maintains temperature monitoring validation and refrigerated core payload metrics
system_message:
You are Thermal systems manager (TSM). As the Thermal systems manager (TSM), you oversee temperature monitoring qualification protocols, continuous logger specifications, and refrigerated core payload capacities across candidate logistics partners.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Maintains temperature monitoring validation and refrigerated core payload metrics（THRMVAL）
information_points.content:
TSM-THRMVAL-0UO：For Polaris CryoLogistics Alliance, continuous temperature logging is validated across consignment active sensor arrays, featuring a continuous logging interval of 2 min across all payload temperature probe channels and a validated refrigerated core payload of 900 kg in the primary sub-zero active cooling compartment.
TSM-THRMVAL-DNX：For AeroMed Global Coldchain, continuous temperature logging is validated across consignment active sensor arrays, operating with a continuous logging interval of 2 min across all payload temperature probe channels. The partner also provides a validated refrigerated core payload of 1,100 kg in its primary sub-zero active cooling compartment.
TSM-THRMVAL-VVP：For Vanguard BioLogistics Network, continuous temperature logging is validated across consignment active sensor arrays, with a continuous logging interval of 10 min across all payload temperature probe channels, and a validated refrigerated core payload of 800 kg in its primary sub-zero active cooling compartment.

information_points.title: Refrigeration pre-cooling（CHILL）
information_points.content:
TSM-CHILL-UX0：For Polaris CryoLogistics Alliance, pre-cooling qualification records document a chamber pull-down time of 60 min to chill standard active transport container internal air from 25 °C down to 4 °C.
TSM-CHILL-DAX：For AeroMed Global Coldchain, pre-cooling qualification runs indicate a chamber pull-down time of 30 min to reduce standard active transport container internal air from 25 °C down to 4 °C.
TSM-CHILL-QPO：For Vanguard BioLogistics Network, pre-cooling qualification runs document a chamber pull-down time of 45 min to lower the standard active transport container internal air temperature from 25 °C to 4 °C.
